newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle trade slow - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle trade slow - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle trade as of late Tuesday afternoon was slow, feedlot sources said.
About 300 lightweight slaughter steers and heifers sold at $68.00 per cwt in the Texas Panhandle/western Oklahoma area, they said, noting the volume was too small to set a trend.
Light packer bids at $68.00 were mostly passed by owners pricing cattle at $70.00, with some at $71.00, cattle feeders said.
Last sales were Thursday and Friday at $69.00, steady with the bulk of trade the previous week.

Attempts to sell cattle at higher prices so far this week have been blunted by sliding beef prices and uncertainty over possible bearish expectations of Friday's USDA Cattle-on-Feed Report, sources said. The report is expected to show larger- than-year-ago numbers of cattle on feed with pre-report analysts' estimates for May 1 cattle on feed ranging from 108 to 111 percent of a year earlier. Placement estimates ranged from 104.9 to 127.5 percent and marketings 98.6 to 104.
Beef prices on Tuesday were quoted down $0.44 to $0.99 per cwt on 374 fabricated loads sold, USDA reported.

Heavyweight choice beef fell $0.75 to $106.35, USDA said. That was down $2.23 from a week ago, USDA statistics showed. However, week-to-date movement reported by USDA at 531 loads was above the previous week's 441.
